historical_changes_found: Rumble oEmbed attached to post.link between 2024-11-06 and 2025-07-29 (YouTube oEmbeds were attached by 2024-10-24 at latest). Effect: video posts since ~2025 yield BOTH video and a linkCard{url:watch page, imageUrl:''}; the site renders no link card for video posts, so the linkCard is spurious (present-day behavior too, not just old).
Rumble thumbnail CDN host changed from 1a-1791.com (seen 2024-10 through 2025-08) to *.cdn.rumble.cloud (seen 2026-09-14). This is the Sep-2026 thumbnail breakage root cause from the Rumble side.

extraction_gaps_confirmed.gap: Old Rumble video posts get video.thumbnail=null
extraction_gaps_confirmed.mechanism: extractVideoThumbnail only matches https://*.cdn.rumble.cloud/... literally, or "thumbnail_url":"..." as a literal JSON pair. Old posts use host 1a-1791.com, and in devalue the pair is "thumbnail_url":<slot> (a numeric reference), so neither regex can match. The URL is recoverable — it sits as a plain string in the devalue slots — but current code never resolves it.

timeMatch / handleMatch / nameMatch href use [\w.] which excludes '-'. '@FloatingOnSmiles-Fos' fails to match, so timestamp/timeAgo are null. username/displayName survive via the payload path. Any-era issue, found on a 2026 post but equally applicable to old posts.

extraction_gaps_confirmed.gap: Spurious imageless linkCard on video posts (payload-derived)
posts: https://pickax.com/post/330000 (counter-example: 2026-05-16 YouTube video post with post.link=null -> NO linkCard, clean)
extraction_gaps_confirmed.mechanism: linkCardFromPost maps post.link unconditionally; for video posts link is the oEmbed object (type:'video') with no 'image' key, yielding {url:watch URL, domain, title, imageUrl:''}. The DOM fallback (requiring img.pickax.com/metadata/) correctly finds no card, but the payload path wins. Present in current behavior as well. Attachment is intermittent: e.g. post 330000 (2026-05-16, YouTube) has post.link=null and yields a clean video-only payload, so the spurious card appears only when the oEmbed happened to be attached.

edge_cases.notes: HTTP 404, 'Post not found' (statusCode 404 in payload). Page is byte-identical to the 404 for never-existed IDs (post 0, post 999999999) apart from the /post/<id> path string — deleted vs never-created are indistinguishable externally. The worker's extract() returns null (no displayName/username/text) -> 404 'not-found', so the tool's reliance on 404 is safe. Other dead IDs sampled: 4000, 15000, 20000, 25000, 40000, 60000, 75000, 95000, 110000, 130000, 160000, 180000, 200000, 220000, 360000.
